contract: C12, the control door: docs/contracts/C12.md (board ab-v16.94.1). One JSON object per line on the service's control.sock. The daemon sends the requests (req); the service sends the answers (res) and the events (ev). Each request carries its provenance (by). The service and the daemon test against the same lines. The service's state for these lines, and the fake's state at its start (agent-browser service --fake): state. Its open prompts are p1 (host login.example, list owner-repo) and p2 (host cdn.example, list owner-repo); its list owner-repo holds a.example and old.example. The reads q1 to q5 give the keys of the data of status, lists_get, prompts_get, endpoint and sender (stage 1a, board ab-v16.94.2). Since board ab-v16.94.5 (stage 1d; the token design, board ab-v16.94.10) each item of set_sessions carries mcp_token, the fingerprint of the session's connection token or null; the bad lines b22 to b32 break each rule of mcp_token; r14 is the daemon's snapshot while two live sessions have one launch name (live: the daemon's live sessions); testTokens are made-up test values in a token's form, with their fingerprints. The stored sign-ins (board ab-v16.97.1, the part "The stored sign-ins" of C12): the requests s1 to s52 run in their order after r14 with the fake values of state.sign_ins (the fake opens no seal), the bad requests b33 to b52 refuse a kind, a shape or a rule of record, unprotected holds the cases of a protection that does not hold (each on a new fake with --unprotected), and signInScan holds the canaries of the scan.

off.agent_text: The agent browser is not running.
off.operator_text: The agent browser is not running. A start on the Browser page starts it.

hellos.note: the hello of agent-browser service --fake (agentwatch's hermetic tests): the features fake, mcp_token and sign_ins
a newer daemon's hello: a field and a feature that the service does not know, which it ignores

badHellos.note: the daemon reads a hello whose side is not service (a process that is not the service, or a mixed-up peer): it closes the connection
the service reads a hello whose side is not daemon: it closes the connection
a hello whose v is not 1 is a new door: the reader closes the connection and sends no request and no answer

refused.note: the systemd query failed (m1): one line with the reason, then the service closes the connection

line.reason: The control door cannot read the MainPID of agentwatch's unit, so it admits no connection.

refused.note: a peer that fails a rule of 1 to 4 (here rule 2: its parent is not the MainPID): one line that names the rule, then the service closes the connection

line.reason: The control door admits only the agentwatch daemon process: rule 2 failed (its parent is not the MainPID of agentwatch's unit).

requests.note: config: agentwatch's browser.* keys as data, at each connect and each change
config with browser.control false: the endpoint and the MCP path answer the 503 of C11

set_sessions: a complete snapshot of four local sessions (each with its lifetime id, or null: shell-2 and web-2 have none), each with its mcp_token (the fingerprint of its connection token: web-1 and tool-4 have one, and a session whose lifetime id is null has null), no remote scope before stage 5, and the box's own sign-in hosts and cookie names

status (the data keys of stage 1a): the state with the agent's text and the operator's text as two keys, Chrome's facts, the endpoint's form, the MCP's state (none before stage 1d), the sessions of r3 (each with mcp_token true or false, never the fingerprint), the lists, no stop yet, and the open prompts with their recipients; the stored sign-ins' state (none, before any op of the store)
lists_get: each list with its repo, its entries, the scopes that use it and its read error, and the old single list
prompts_get: the open prompts, each with its recipients (the session name and the lifetime id of each session that a block stopped; web-2's lifetime id is null, and web-2 is still a recipient)
endpoint: the endpoint's URL for the scope
sender: the sender's ID, its version and its package (here the fake's empty zip)
session_ended
launch_check of a name that is free
launch_check of a name whose ended scope is held in memory only

data.refusal: A session named web-1 ended a moment ago, and the agent browser could not record it (the file of ended scopes cannot be written: ENOSPC). Choose another name, or wait until the agent browser confirms its lists.

badLines.note: a line that starts with a byte order mark (EF BB BF): not a compact line; it closes the connection
a line that ends in CR LF: a CR breaks the compact-line rule; it closes the connection
a line with the bytes of a lone surrogate (ED A0 80) in a string: not UTF-8; it closes the connection

testTokensNote: Made-up test values in the form of a connection token (abt1_ and 43 base64url characters, 32 bytes; the token design): the bytes of each one are its own ASCII label, so none is a real token. fingerprint: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the token's ASCII bytes, as set_sessions carries it. The door never carries a token: b24 shows a token in place of its fingerprint, which is a bad request.

signInScan.note: The canaries of the stored sign-ins' scan (fake values): no line of these vectors holds one in a form of the guard (plain, URL-encoded, JSON-escaped, base64, base64url).

unprotected.note: The cases of a protection of the service's memory that does not hold (C12, the stored sign-ins: the protections; the design, section 5.5). Each case runs on a new fake with --unprotected <reason>, in its order on one connection after the hellos; sign_ins is the key of status after its requests.
